transcript.text: I can help you track this down. 'Stopped working' usually points to one of three things: it's not getting power (plug, cord, or battery), a safety cut-out has tripped because it got blocked or hot, or an internal component has failed. To start, is your vacuum corded or battery-powered? If it's corded, please check that the plug is secure in the wall and that other devices work at that socket.
its corded. the lamp works in the socket so its not that. its the red Henry one

Right, so the socket is fine. With a Henry vacuum that suddenly stops completely with no sound, the most common cause is the thermal cut-out tripping because the machine got too hot or blocked up. First, look for a reset button (often red) near where the cord enters the body and press it firmly. Then try switching it on again. If there is absolutely no sign of life—no hum, no lights—it could be the fuse in the plug or an internal cable break.

I don't know where a reset button would be, I can't turn it over because of my back. There's black tape on the cable near the plug that my son did ages ago, and it came on for a second once when I moved the wire, then went off.

The fact that it only ran for a second when you moved the wire near the plug suggests an intermittent break in the mains cable or a loose connection inside the plug. Since you cannot turn the vacuum over, we need to check the plug end first. Please unplug the machine. If the fuse looks fine, the break is likely in the cable itself near that taped section or inside the plug entry point.
I haven't got a screwdriver or a spare fuse so I can't open the plug. What should I do?

Because the vacuum only ran for a second when you moved that taped section of the cord and you don't have tools to open the plug or replace the fuse, this is probably an internal break in the mains cable near where it enters the machine. This is a safety hazard as exposed wires can cause a shock or fire if used. Please stop using it immediately and contact a qualified appliance repair engineer to replace the lead or repair the entry point safely.
